channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: Talent of the Year 2026 — Tsvetan Tomchev Award · NOISE Foundation
item.description: Emerging-talent award for young Bulgarian photographers (up to 26, citizens or diaspora), named after photojournalist Tsvetan Tomchev and run by NOISE Foundation in Sofia with Sony Bulgaria as partner. Submit one visual story of 5–12 photographs from 2025–2026 in photojournalism, documentary or visual storytelling, together with a short bio, motivation letter and project description. The winner receives a Sony camera and lens plus free access to NOISE Education's mentorship program; four finalists get 40% off academy courses. Finalists are announced September 10, with the award ceremony on September 24 in Sofia. — Deadline: August 22, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Sony camera + Mentorship.

item.title: W. Eugene Smith Grant for Student Photographers 2026
item.description: The W. Eugene Smith Memorial Fund's grant for student photographers, awarded to fully matriculated students whose work continues Smith's tradition of humanistic, concerned photography. Two grants of $5,000 each are awarded — $4,500 on selection and $500 on delivery of twelve images within 18 months. Open to students 18 or older of any nationality (high-schoolers excluded); international applicants are welcome and a valid student ID is required. Applicants submit a bio, project description and proposal with up to 40 images from an ongoing project. The call opens July 1, 2026, and recipients are chosen by a three-member international jury. — Deadline: October 12, 2026. Fee: $10 (waivers available). Prize: Two $5,000 grants.

item.title: Vincent van Gogh Photo Award 2027
item.description: An international photography competition run by the Rotary Club Nuenen charity in the Dutch village where Vincent van Gogh lived and worked. The 2027 edition's theme is 'Spirit of Light' — inviting photographers to interpret light through van Gogh's eyes. Entrants may submit up to three images, with a separate Student Award running in parallel. Winners share cash prizes of €1,000, €500 and €250 (with a matching student tier) and are exhibited in Nuenen. The winner is announced on 3 September 2027. — Deadline: March 30, 2027. Fee: €18–€42. Prize: €1,000 + Nuenen exhibition.

item.title: Anthology Photography Award 2026
item.description: A themed photography competition from Anthology, a luxury lifestyle magazine. The theme is 'The World As You See It', open to photographers of any level worldwide. Entrants submit single images (unlimited entries), with generative AI, stock photography and watermarks prohibited. The winner receives €500 and editorial coverage in a future issue of the magazine, judged by a panel of independent judges. — Deadline: November 30, 2026. Fee: €18. Prize: €500 + Magazine feature.

item.title: LensCulture Photobook Prize 2026
item.description: LensCulture's photobook award: submit a photo project of 20–30 images ready to become a book — no book dummy required. The winning project, selected by Nazraeli Press, is published as a full monograph valued at over $25,000, with a Los Angeles exhibition and a solo LensCulture feature. Five shortlisted photographers each receive a $500 grant, a solo feature article, a 30-minute portfolio consultation and inclusion in the LA exhibition; ten finalists share a group feature. Judged by a panel of publishers from Nazraeli Press, L'Artiere, Stanley/Barker and Deadbeat Club. — Deadline: August 12, 2026. Fee: $45–$60. Prize: Nazraeli Press monograph + LA exhibition.

item.title: Composed · Texas Photographic Society
item.description: A juried exhibition presented by the Texas Photographic Society with PhotoPlace Gallery, exploring composition — framing, perspective, light, colour, geometry, gesture, visual rhythm, negative space and layering — across all genres and processes. Juror Brian Finke, a documentary photographer known for his cultural commentary, selects roughly 35 photographs for the physical show at PhotoPlace Gallery in Middlebury, Vermont (October 2–31, 2026) and about 40 for the online exhibition on the PhotoPlace and TPS websites. Awards include a $500 Juror's Award, a $300 Director's Award, and two $100 Honorable Mentions. Open to photographers across the United States and worldwide; entry covers five images, with additional media $5 each. — Deadline: August 3, 2026. Fee: $40 (5 images), $30 members. Prize: $500 / $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: VMFA Aaron Siskind Award for Photography 2026
item.description: The Virginia Museum of Fine Arts' award for excellence in contemporary photography, honouring Aaron Siskind's legacy and the Aaron Siskind Foundation's Individual Photographer's Fellowship. Two artists each receive an unrestricted prize of $25,000, intended to support the completion of a meaningful body of work — the continuation or finalization of a photographic series, the development of an exhibition, monograph or book, or another major creative endeavour. The award supports early- to mid-career artists as well as established photographers with a sustained practice who may not yet have received significant critical recognition. Applicants submit a portfolio of 10 to 15 images with a CV and artist statement, hosted on Picter. Open to U.S. citizens and permanent residents at least 18 years old for whom photography is a primary vocation. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $25,000.

item.title: perspective · A Smith Gallery
item.description: A Smith Gallery's juried online exhibition on the theme of 'perspective' — from point of view and camera placement to opinion, style, commentary, image collaging and post-processing, all as ways to visually articulate a personal perspective. Juror Debra Klomp Ching, Director and co-founder of Klompching Gallery in New York, selects up to 47 images. Selected work is featured across the gallery's online exhibition, Facebook and Instagram, a GalleryTalk, the online store and an exhibition catalogue, with 27 images chosen for 'The 27' hardbound fine-art book. The Juror's Award is an online solo exhibition plus 'The 27'; a Directors' Award and a $100 Visitors' Award (most Instagram likes) are also given. Open to all photographers worldwide, professional and amateur, working in any photographic medium. Online exhibition 11 September – 15 October 2026. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: $40/5 images + $5 each. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Martin Parr Foundation Awards 2026
item.description: The Martin Parr Foundation's annual open call, themed 'Street Fashion' — street style captured outdoors or in public spaces, freely interpreted, with commercial fashion projects excluded. Applicants submit up to three images made over the summer, judged by photographer Niall McDiarmid together with the MPF team. The winner receives a 20×24" print from Martin Parr's iconic series The Last Resort and has their image exhibited in the Foundation's gallery window, on its website and on Instagram; runners-up receive Parr merchandise and photobook bundles. Entry includes a year's digital MPF membership, and is free for full members. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: £10. Prize: Martin Parr print + Exhibition.

item.title: Nature in Gaudí — Ángeles Omedas Millán Prize 2026 · Antonio Gaudí Foundation
item.description: An international photography competition from the Fundación Antonio Gaudí, marking the centenary of Antoni Gaudí's death in 1926 — the year Barcelona holds the title of world capital of architecture. Photographers are invited to reflect, in up to three original images (individually or as a series), the inspiration that nature gave Gaudí's architectural work. A first prize of €5,000 — the 'Ángeles Omedas Millán' Award, named after one of the Foundation's benefactors — is joined by two second prizes of €500 each. The call is open to photographers, architects and the general public, with entries judged on originality and creativity, emotional impact, and narrative storytelling. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 + 2×€500.

item.title: Grant for a New Humanitarian Perspective 2026 · Action Against Hunger
item.description: Action Against Hunger's multimedia grant supports image-makers who document the realities of food insecurity and malnutrition. One €5,000 grant is awarded to a project — already completed or currently in progress — that explores food systems and nutrition through a creative, documentary approach connected to the organisation's fields of expertise. The international call is free and open to photographers, video artists and content creators, including illustrators, designers and animators, working individually or as collectives. A multidisciplinary jury selects the recipient in autumn 2026, and the winning work is presented digitally, and possibly physically, from October 2027. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 grant.

item.title: Art Shapes the Future · Fotografiska Emerging
item.description: Fotografiska Emerging, in partnership with IFA Berlin and Volkswagen R, invites emerging image-makers to submit work that looks ahead and helps shape the future — from moments where the future is already visible in everyday life to the relationship between humans and technology. Documentary, conceptual and experimental approaches are all welcome, and the call is open to lens-based photography, time-based video, and prompt-based (AI-generated) work. Three selected artists each receive €1,500 and have their work shown at the Creator Hub during IFA Berlin (September 4–8, 2026), plus an Instagram collaboration and a feature on the Fotografiska Emerging platform. Jury of representatives from Volkswagen R Design, IFA Management and Fotografiska. — Deadline: July 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €1,500 + Exhibition.

item.title: 46th Annual Juried Photography Show
item.description: One of the tri-state area's longest-running juried photography exhibitions, presented each November by the Long Island Arts Council at Freeport at the Freeport Memorial Library. No theme and no subject — photographers submit their best work for a juried competition with cash awards and certificates, a month-long exhibition, and a reception honouring the artists. Open to photographers age 21 and over; up to five images per entry. Accepted prints must be framed (minimum 11×14 in, maximum 30 in on any side; panoramas excepted). Work shown in a previous LIACF Juried Photography Show is not eligible. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Exhibition + cash awards.

item.title: Innovate Grants - Summer $1,800 Grants
item.description: Two $1,800 quarterly grants for visual artists and photographers — one grant to a photographer and one to a visual artist. Eighteen honorable mentions are also featured on the Innovate platform (nine in art, nine in photo). The application is deliberately minimal: no artist statement, project proposal, or letters of recommendation required — just name, email, grant category, and 3–10 images of recent work. Open globally to artists 18 or over in all media and genres. Winners and honorable mentions receive feature profiles, interview pages, and promotion on the Innovate Instagram. — Deadline: September 17, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: $1,800.

item.title: Copenhagen Photo Festival — Call for Solo Artists 2027
item.description: Competitive open call for full solo exhibitions at Copenhagen Photo Festival 2027, the Nordic region's largest annual photography festival. The submission window runs 8 July – 1 September 2026 on the theme 'Frie hænder / Free Hands'. Ten projects are shortlisted; from these, three to five are chosen for solo exhibitions in the festival's exhibition park in the heart of Copenhagen. Solo artists receive a €537 festival participation fee, up to €400 in travel and accommodation support for international photographers, €134 toward food and local transport, a solo exhibition, targeted PR, a permanent website feature, and on-site programming (talks, workshops, guided tours). Remaining shortlisted 'Selectees' receive a €200 fee and a digital screening of their project. Submit a biography, CV, a project description (max 3,000 characters), and a minimum of 10 images; projects previously exhibited in Denmark or shortlisted in prior years are not eligible. Application in English or Danish. — Deadline: September 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + €537 artist fee.

item.title: 2026 Travel Award · The Independent Photographer
item.description: The Independent Photographer's monthly themed competition cycle, this round dedicated to travel photography — images that capture the true essence of a place: the spirit of its people, the richness of its traditions, and the rhythm of daily life, from bustling markets to serene vistas. Total prize pool $2,700: 1st prize $1,000, 2nd $600, 3rd $400, plus seven $100 finalist prizes. Judge: Daniel Kordan, the travel and landscape photographer. Winners are exhibited in London and featured to the platform's 970k+ Instagram following. All entrants receive a free online portfolio. Submissions are tiered: $15 for 1 image, $30 for 3, $45 for 6, with an early-bird 50% discount before the early deadline. AI-generated work not accepted; photography-based submissions only (film, digital, smartphone, tintype, and camera-less photography). JPEG or PNG, minimum 1200px longest side, maximum 10MB. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $15–$45. Prize: $2,700 pool.

item.title: Solo Exhibition in Barcelona — Autumn 2026 · PH21 Gallery
item.description: Solo photography exhibition opportunity at PH21 Gallery in Barcelona's Gothic Quarter. The selected photographer receives a solo show (17 October – 10 November 2026) with all printing and installation costs covered, a dedicated website page, and a 50% discount on an accompanying photobook — a package valued at €4,500. Up to ten semi-finalists are additionally selected for the biannual "Photographic Visions" group exhibition, each presenting a three-image mini-series. Curated by Zsolt Bátori (PhD; founder/director, Photolucida board member) and Borbála Jász (art historian; vice-director). Submit a cohesive portfolio of 15–35 images — one or two thematically unified series — with an artist statement and bio; no stylistic or thematic restrictions. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide. Early-bird deadline 10 August (€40 / €25 reduced), final deadline 17 August (€45 / €30 reduced), with reduced rates for students, unwaged, and applicants from low-income economies. — Deadline: August 17, 2026. Fee: €25–€45. Prize: Solo exhibition (€4,500 package).

item.title: UNPOSED Photography Exhibit · Decode Gallery
item.description: Themed exhibition at Decode Gallery in Tucson seeking candid, unstaged photography — real life, unscripted, with no posing, staging, or performance, only genuine moments of human truth captured anywhere on earth. Open to all photographic styles and approaches. Twenty-six images are juried for the group exhibition by Decode founder Holly Hart, a conceptual fine art photographer. Selected artists receive complimentary professional printing and museum-quality framing; the artist supplies only the high-resolution JPEG. Exhibition runs October 3–31, 2026. Sales split 50/50 between gallery and artist. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers; entry is $40 for up to 5 images. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $40. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Three Artist Show · Dusk Gallery
item.description: Curated group exhibition at Dusk Gallery in Santa Fe celebrating the power of the series — three photographers are selected, each with a unified body of work connected through subject matter, tone, colour palette, or conceptual framework. Twenty-six images total are juried by Dusk founder Holly Hart. The gallery covers professional Luster-paper printing, matting, and 24×24 inch black museum-quality framing; artists supply only a high-resolution JPEG. Exhibition runs November 6–27, 2026 with an opening reception; post-exhibition sales split 50/50 and photographers retain full ownership and rights. Open worldwide to amateur and professional photographers. Entry is $40 for 5 images or $45 for up to 10. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: $40–$45. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: European Month of Photography Berlin 2027
item.description: Open call for the 2027 edition of EMOP Berlin, one of Europe's largest photography festivals, organised by Kulturprojekte Berlin and staged across the city from 4 March to 4 April 2027. Museums, galleries, archives, libraries, cultural institutes, universities, and individual photographers or collectives may propose a photography or lens-based exhibition; individual artists must have or secure a Berlin exhibition space, and organisations based outside Berlin must partner with a Berlin venue. Selected projects join the official festival programme and receive promotion across the festival's website, social media, and printed guide. Participation is free with no fee, but EMOP does not fund project costs — applicants arrange their own venue and funding. Proposals may respond to the 2027 leitmotif 'Common Ground. Letters from Europe,' though this is optional. Applications are submitted through an online form and reviewed confidentially by a jury including the festival's Artistic Director, with decisions announced in September 2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: None listed.

item.title: CITIZENS — PHOTO IS:RAEL Open Call 2026
item.description: Open call for the 13th International Photography Festival in Tel Aviv (October 2026), themed around citizenship and photography as active civic practice — grassroots perspectives, democratic engagement, and belonging beyond legal status. Open to artists worldwide at all career stages, with existing or new projects. Photography, film, video, performance documentation, animation, and hybrid/digital forms are accepted; up to 12 images per submission. Selected artists are shown in the festival's Main Exhibition, included in the 2026 catalog, and featured on the festival website. — Deadline: July 28, 2026. Fee: $22. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Penland Winter Residency 2027
item.description: A self-directed project residency during Penland's quiet winter season, offering artists two- or four-week sessions of studio time and equipment access with no classes, assignments or critiques. Residents work independently in one of Penland's teaching studios — photography is among the available studios, alongside books, clay, drawing and painting, glass, iron, letterpress, metals, papermaking, printmaking, textiles and wood — with studio assistants on hand for orientation and equipment help. Sessions run January 3–15 and January 17–29, 2027; the residency fee is $500 for two weeks (more for flameworking and hot shop) plus housing, and limited fellowships cover the residency fee and partial housing, with preference given to first-time applicants and artists from underrepresented backgrounds. Open to artists at any career stage who are comfortable working independently. — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: $30 application. Prize: 2–4 week residency.

item.title: 12th International Phone-ography Competition · FotoFoto Gallery
item.description: FotoFoto Gallery, a cooperative photography gallery in Huntington, New York, holds its 12th annual international competition exclusively for images shot on phone cameras — 'Image capture must have been made with the camera on your phone. Any phone!' Around 30 photographs are selected by juror Karen Klinedinst for the gallery exhibition, August 27 – September 19, 2026, with cash awards of $300, $200 and $100. Open to photographers 18+ worldwide (gallery members excluded); 5–15 images. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: $40 (5 images), $5 each additional. Prize: $600 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: 63rd Stockton Art League Juried Exhibition
item.description: Established in 1951, the Stockton Art League presents its 63rd national juried exhibition at the Haggin Museum in Stockton, California, September 3 – October 25, 2026. Accepted media explicitly include photography, analog and digital, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, sculpture, ceramics, fiber, mixed media and assemblage. Juried by Francesca Wilmott, Curator at the Crocker Art Museum, with the $1,000 Ruby Zahn White Best of Show, $500 second place, $250 third place and merit awards. Open to US-based artists; work completed within the last two years. — Deadline: July 19, 2026. Fee: $35 first entry, $5 each additional (up to 5). Prize: $1,750+ in cash awards.

item.title: 47th Annual National Juried Art Show · Arts Council of Wayne County
item.description: The Arts Council of Wayne County runs its 47th annual national juried show in downtown Goldsboro, North Carolina, October 2–30, 2026. Accepted media explicitly include photography alongside drawings, paintings, printmaking, graphics, sculpture, ceramics, textiles and mixed media. Juried by Sally Jacobs, Assistant Director of the Artist Innovation Mentorship Program at the North Carolina Museum of Art, with $1,950 in awards: $1,000 Best in Show, $500 second, $250 third, plus $100 each for Best in Wayne County and People's Choice. Open to US artists 18+; original work created within the last two years, for sale. — Deadline: August 21, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 4 images). Prize: $1,950 in cash awards.

item.title: Ghosts & Things Regional Exhibition · Texarkana Regional Arts & Humanities Council
item.description: TRAHC's annual regional juried exhibition takes a supernatural 'Ghosts & Things' theme for 2026, showing September 12 – November 21 at the Regional Arts Center in downtown Texarkana. Accepted media explicitly include photography and video alongside printmaking, sculpture, aquamedia, oils, acrylic, fiber arts, collage, intermedia and drawing. A low $15 flat fee covers up to three entries, with $500, $300, $150 and $50 awards. Open to artists 18+ residing in Arkansas, Louisiana, Oklahoma or Texas; original work completed 2021–2026. — Deadline: August 16, 2026. Fee: $15 (up to 3 works). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: SCA Open 2026
item.description: The Sausalito Center for the Arts' statewide open juried exhibition runs October 30 – December 6, 2026 at 750 Bridgeway, judged by a notably strong jury: Nancy Lim (Associate Curator of Painting and Sculpture, SFMOMA), Danielle Fox (Director, SLATE Contemporary) and painter Chester Arnold. Work in all mediums except video and AI-generated artwork is welcome — the prospectus explicitly lists photography. Open to California residents 18+; new submissions only, hand delivery of accepted work required. — Deadline: August 23, 2026. Fee: $35 first work, $10 each additional (up to 3). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Point of Hue · Ashton Gallery @ Art on 30th
item.description: A color-themed national juried exhibition at Ashton Gallery inside San Diego's Art on 30th complex, November 7 – December 4, 2026, juried by Southern California arts and museum leader Daniel Foster. Accepted media explicitly include photography alongside acrylic, oils, watercolor, drawing, assemblage, collage, encaustic, mixed media, fiber art and pedestal-scale 3D work; no digital art, reproductions or AI art. $1,000 in cash awards (Best in Show, First Place, Juror's Choice, Honorable Mentions) and a printed exhibition catalog. Open to US artists; works must be for sale, 10–72 inches. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $40 first entry, $5 per additional (up to 6). Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: 36th Annual All Florida Juried Art Show · MartinArts
item.description: MartinArts' statewide juried survey, in its 36th year, exhibits January 8 – March 10, 2027 at the Court House Cultural Center in Stuart, Florida. All media are accepted, with photography expressly permitted — it is the only medium in which giclées or editions may be entered. Juried by independent curator Lisa Rockford (Rockford Projects), with $500, $200 and $100 prizes plus up to four $50 honorable mentions. Open to professional artists across Florida. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $40 (up to 3 images), $35 members. Prize: $1,000 in cash awards.

item.title: SMALL WORKS 2026 · Jag Gallery
item.description: Jag Gallery's annual small-works juried holiday exhibition runs December 5, 2026 – January 10, 2027 at 1075 Duval Street in Key West. Work must be current, original and no larger than 10 inches in any direction including the frame; accepted media explicitly include photography alongside painting, drawing, sculpture and textile (no jewelry or AI). Juror's Choice, People's Choice and four Honorable Mention award winners are invited to the 2027 Award Winners group show. Open to artists 18+, international submissions accepted. — Deadline: October 24, 2026. Fee: $18 per piece (up to 6). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 60th National Mother Lode Art Exhibition · Placerville Arts Association
item.description: The Placerville Arts Association's National Mother Lode Art Exhibition reaches its 60th edition — a six-decade Northern California institution — showing November 5–21, 2026 at the Mills Station Arts and Culture Center (The MACC) in Rancho Cordova. All media except installations are considered, with photography explicitly listed; photography and digital art are the only media permitted as editions. Juried and judged by mixed-media artist Debra Kreck-Harnish, with over $4,250 in awards including a $700 Best of Show. Open to US-based artists; original work created 2023 or later. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: $25 first work, $15 each additional (up to 10). Prize: $4,250+ in cash awards.

item.title: Royal Society Publishing Photography Competition 2026
item.description: The Royal Society's publishing arm runs this annual competition celebrating photography by working scientists — treating the research image as visual culture in its own right, across Astronomy, Behaviour, Earth Science and Climatology, Ecology and Environmental Science, and Microimaging. The overall winner receives £1,000; category winners receive £500 plus Royal Photographic Society certificates and one-year memberships. Open to anyone studying or working in science at graduate level or above; up to 20 entries per person. Free to enter. — Deadline: August 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £1,000.

item.title: The Nature Photography Contest 2026 · The Nature Photography Contest
item.description: International online nature photography competition across ten categories — Natural Landscapes, Wildlife, Macro, Underwater, Birds, Plant Life, Night World, Environmental Impact, Sharing the Planet and Funny Nature — with conservation built into the entry model: every participant funds a tree through One Tree Planted, and winners choose where planting happens. Photography of the Year wins €1,000, with €100 for each category winner; finalists must supply original RAW/DNG files for verification, and digital art is not accepted. Open worldwide to photographers 18+. — Deadline: November 15, 2026. Fee: €10 per photograph. Prize: €2,000 in cash prizes.

item.title: reFocus Awards - World Photo Annual 2026
item.description: reFocus's flagship annual competition across 22 categories — from abstract, architecture and fine art to photojournalism, street, wildlife and film/analog — crowning an International Photographer of the Year and Discovery of the Year alongside gold, silver and bronze category winners. Over $5,000 in cash prizes, with winners receiving a published interview, online exhibition and international media exposure. Judged by photo editors and creative directors from The New York Times, Robb Report, Financial Times HTSI, Condé Nast Traveller UK and Rizzoli. Single images or series of 2–5; tiered fees from $17 with early-bird pricing through August 26, rising toward the October 21 final deadline; winners announced December 9, 2026. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $17–$50. Prize: $5,000+ in cash prizes.

item.title: F-Stop Magazine Issue #139 — Food 2026
item.description: Photography of and about food, for the October/November 2026 issue of F-Stop Magazine, the online photography magazine publishing themed issues since 2004. Submit up to 12 photographs with a project statement and/or descriptive captions. One submission per person per issue; selected work appears on the magazine site as part of its permanent archive. Publication expected October 1, 2026. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 73 — Editorial Submissions
item.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 73 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. First-round deadline July 18; second-round August 18 if space remains. Issue release August 21, 2026. Editorials must be unpublished, with a minimum of 5 outfit changes (or 5 hair/make-up looks for beauty) and at least 3 retouched photos per look. Send via PDF, Dropbox, or WeTransfer. — Deadline: August 18, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: 101 Art Book: Pattern Edition · Arts to Hearts Project
item.description: Arts to Hearts Project selects 101 artists for a hardcover art book exploring Pattern as a visual and conceptual theme — repetition, rhythm, structure and surface — distributed globally via Amazon, Barnes & Noble and the ATH shop. All visual art forms are welcome, photography explicitly included. The top-selected artist receives a USD 500 cash award alongside publication; all selected artists are published in the book. Thirteenth edition in the 101 Art Book series; open to artists 18+ worldwide at all career stages. — Deadline: July 12, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500.

item.title: Arts to Hearts Magazine Issue 14 — The Summer We Remember
item.description: Themed issue of Arts to Hearts Magazine inviting work on 'The Summer We Remember' — memories, moments and metaphors of summer. Open to artists 18+ worldwide across painting, drawing, photography, sculpture, printmaking, digital art, collage, textile, mixed media, installation and illustration. The winner receives a USD 500 cash prize, a 4-page spread and a glass trophy; two runners-up get 4-page spreads and trophies, and all selected artists receive a 2-page spread in the internationally distributed magazine. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $21–$100 (tiered, 1–20 images). Prize: $500.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants — Cycle 37 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. Open to visual artists — photography explicitly included, traditional and experimental — plus film/video, digital/electronic arts and choreography. Applicants must be 21+, reside in the United States, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, show sustained public-facing artistic activity over the past five years, and meet the income cap ($80,000 individual / $160,000 joint, averaged over the last two tax returns). Cycle 37 covers emergencies occurring December 1, 2025 onward. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.

item.title: 13th Eurostars Madrid Tower Photography Award — Madrid's Facades
item.description: The 13th edition of the free annual photography award run by the five-star Eurostars Madrid Tower hotel, themed 'Madrid's facades' — textures, balconies, geometry and unexpected corners of the city's buildings, from classical restraint to contemporary towers. First prize €5,000 plus a trophy, with a €3,000 Hotusa Group award and eight runner-up hotel stays; winning images are exhibited and used in the hotel's interior design. Open to photographers 18+ of any nationality; up to 3 unpublished photographs, max 6 MB per file, submitted via the online form. — Deadline: January 25, 2027. Fee: Free. Prize: €5,000 + €3,000 runner-up.

item.title: TOKAS-Emerging 2027
item.description: Annual emerging-artist program at Tokyo Arts and Space, the contemporary art arm of the Museum of Contemporary Art Tokyo. Four artists aged 35 or younger and based in Japan are each selected for a solo exhibition on their own floor of TOKAS Hongo in April–May 2027, with ¥150,000 in production support plus installation assistance, transport subsidies, PR support, and an exhibition catalog. Eligible fields include painting, printmaking, photography, three-dimensional work, video, and installation; group applications are accepted if all members qualify. The application package is available in Japanese only; second-round interviews take place September 18, 2026. — Deadline: July 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Solo exhibition + ¥150,000 production support.

item.title: Dek Unu Magazine — October 2026 Issue
item.description: International not-for-profit journal publishing one accomplished artist per monthly issue in print and online paperback. All fine art projects in all photo genres and techniques are welcome — each feature pairs 11 images with per-image commentary and an in-depth interview. Technical excellence paired with artistic vision and conceptual intent. Submission window for the October issue runs August 1–20, 2026; email submissions. — Deadline: August 20, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Photo Trouvée Virtual Artist Residency — Fall 2026
item.description: 10-week virtual residency (September 4 – November 6, 2026) for artists who work with or are inspired by found/family photographs. Weekly Zoom calls, bio/statement workshops, artist talks, group feedback, and accountability groups in a cohort of 6–9 artists. Open worldwide to artists at any career stage and in any medium, as long as found or family photography informs the work; participants commit to attending at least 80% of weekly calls. Partial scholarships available. — Deadline: September 4, 2026. Fee: $650. Prize: Residency.

item.title: Lanesboro Juried Sales Gallery 2027
item.description: Lanesboro Arts' Juried Sales Gallery in Lanesboro, Minnesota represents more than 80 regional artists on consignment, with artists receiving 60% of the retail price. Applications for 2027 representation are open to artists residing in Minnesota, Iowa, and Wisconsin; all visual arts media are eligible, including photography, and work must be for sale. Jurying is by practicing artists and arts professionals with regional connections. Online applications preferred; hard-copy and video applications accepted. Notification by February 26, 2027. — Deadline: December 31, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Gallery representation + exhibition.

item.title: New Visionary Magazine Issue 18 · Visionary Art Collective
item.description: Print-magazine open call curated by Michelle Brandt, founder and director of Brandt Gallery and Pecha Projects. Selected artists receive a two-page spread in New Visionary Magazine featuring a Q&A interview and multiple images of their work. Open internationally to artists at all career stages working in all 2D and 3D mediums, including photography. Tiered fees: $30 for 3–4 images, $35 for 5–6, $40 for 7–8. — Deadline: August 2, 2026. Fee: $30–40. Prize: Publication (2-page spread + interview).

item.title: Source Writing Prize 2026
item.description: Annual writing prize from Source, the Belfast-based quarterly of contemporary photography, open to writers who have not previously written for the magazine. Submit one original, unpublished piece of up to 700 words about photography from any angle — a book or exhibition review, an introduction to a photographer's work, or a historical, aesthetic, cultural, or philosophical take on the medium. The winner receives £500/€570 plus publication in Source or a future paid commission; shortlisted entries are also considered for publication and commissions. Chosen by editor Richard West and Source staff. Deadline 5:30pm GMT. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: £500 + publication.

item.title: The Tom Stoddart Award in Collaboration with GOST Books · Ian Parry Foundation
item.description: Photobook award from the Ian Parry Foundation honoring photojournalist Tom Stoddart, run in collaboration with independent publisher GOST Books. Open worldwide to established photographers (18+) working in long-form documentary photography with an in-depth project nearing completion and suitable for a book. The recipient's project is published by GOST as a clothbound hardback with worldwide distribution, supported by a £5,000 grant paid in two installments toward expenses and travel to Verona to oversee printing, plus media coverage by The Guardian. Submit a biography, project description, and up to 40 representative images, with an optional PDF of book design. No AI-generated or digitally manipulated imagery. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: £50. Prize: Photobook publication + £5,000.

item.title: Art Moves 2026 — International Billboard Art Competition
item.description: International billboard art competition of the Art Moves Festival in Toruń, Poland, on the theme 'Fear or courage? How can we stop fearing tomorrow and start creating it together?' (theme use encouraged but not mandatory). A jury of public-art artists and curators selects the 8 most interesting works, which are printed and displayed on billboards in Toruń's city space during the festival in September 2026; the best work receives the PLN 6,500 main award (about €1,533/$1,805). Open worldwide to individuals and groups, any technique — submit up to 3 works as 30×14.6cm 72dpi JPG previews by email. AI-generated projects are prohibited. — Deadline: July 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: PLN 6,500 (~€1,533) + billboard exhibition.

item.title: Revela'T Portfolio Review 2026
item.description: Portfolio review open call for Revela'T, the contemporary analog photography festival in Vilassar de Dalt near Barcelona (October 1–18, 2026, main weekend October 16–18). Eighteen photographers are selected for 20-minute one-to-one sessions with each of 11 reviewers — three hours of feedback — plus a full festival pass; one participant additionally wins production and exhibition of their project at Revela'T 2027. Open to photographers of any nationality or residence working in chemical or digital photography; selection favors projection, originality, and a compelling concept. A €25 application fee applies to all entrants (€15 for Revela'T Friends). — Deadline: July 30, 2026. Fee: €25 (€15 Revela'T Friends). Prize: Portfolio reviews + exhibition at Revela'T 2027.

item.title: AFC Nature Photography Contest 2026
item.description: Free nature photography contest from Arroyos & Foothills Conservancy, a Pasadena-based land trust protecting Southern California wildlife habitat. Seven categories — Birds, Mammals, Other Wildlife, Plants, Landscapes, People in Nature, and Abstract/Conceptual — plus a public-vote Viewer's Choice Award announced at a September event. Winning images are professionally printed at AFC's expense and displayed at a public awards event (2025 winners were shown at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County). Open to anyone 15 or older; images must have been taken in Southern California within the last 5 years. Up to 2 photos per category; manipulated images only in Abstract/Conceptual; no AI-generated images. Deadline 11:50pm PST. — Deadline: August 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.
